Walkthrough

The hydration gate now marks its promise fulfilled when it resolves. When `reactUse` is available, `HydrationGate` passes the promise to it on each render. Tests cover promise status and browser hydration. **Changes: Hydration gate behavior** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |:---|:---| |**Set resolved gate promise status**
`packages/start-client-core/src/hydration/runtime.ts`, `packages/start-client-core/tests/hydration-runtime.test.ts`|The gate sets its promise status to `fulfilled` and its value to `undefined` before calling the resolver. The test checks the status before and after resolution.| |**Use the gate promise on each render**
`packages/react-start-client/src/GenericHydrate.tsx`, `packages/react-start-client/src/tests/HydrateUse.test.tsx`, `.changeset/quiet-gates-hydrate.md`|When `reactUse` is available, `HydrationGate` passes it the gate promise on each render. Without `reactUse`, it throws the promise only while the gate is unresolved. A browser hydration test checks that the child remains rendered and no recoverable error occurs. The changeset declares patch releases for both packages.| **Estimated code review effort:** 2 (Simple) | ~12 minutes **Change:** Bug fix · **Severity of issue fixed:** Low **Possibly related issues** - `#8487` concerns the same React 19 conditional `use()` warning in `lazyRouteComponent` and `Lazy`. This change addresses `HydrationGate`, not those code paths. **Suggested reviewers:** `schiller-manuel`, `sheraff`
Merge Risk: Minimal · up to fc364

This change removes React 19's conditional use() warning in the hydration gate and leaves the React 18 behavior unchanged. No merge-blocking risk is evident. Tests cover the status marking and browser hydration.

Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title names the fix (keep calling use() after a hydration gate resolves) and the affected area (react-start). The changeset covers exactly this: HydrationGate now calls reactUse after the gate resolves, and gate.resolve() marks the promise fulfilled. The title describes the main change.
Full details: Description check

**Explanation** The description covers the change, the motivation, and the test coverage. It links issue `#8997`, explains the React 19 conditional use() warning, and names the two code changes. It also notes the known Lazy follow-up (`#8487`). The Changes section uses short bullets, and the checklist and release impact sections follow the template. The third checklist item (understanding the AI-generated code) is unchecked. The description does not explicitly state the React 19.3 warning appears in a version the workspace does not use, but it does say so. The description is mostly complete.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** Issue `#8997` requires that HydrationGate call use() on every client render after a suspended render, and that a resolved gate never suspend. The diff in packages/react-start-client/src/GenericHydrate.tsx now calls reactUse(props.gate.promise) whenever reactUse is available, including after resolution. The React 18 path throws the promise only while the gate is unresolved, so a resolved gate returns children. In packages/start-client-core/src/hydration/runtime.ts, gate.resolve() sets promise.status = 'fulfilled' and promise.value = undefined before resolvePromise(), so use() does not suspend on a resolved gate that React has not tracked. The PR adds tests for both behaviors (HydrateUse.test.tsx and hydration-runtime.test.ts). The `#8487` Lazy warning is out of scope, as the PR description and the objectives state. Caveat: the React console warning itself was not run. The evidence is the code path and the test assertions on use() calls, which the PR states are the intended check.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check

**Explanation** All changed files map to the linked objective. GenericHydrate.tsx contains the use() ordering change. runtime.ts contains the synchronous fulfilled-status marking. The test files cover both behaviors. The changeset .changeset/quiet-gates-hydrate.md is the release note for the published packages the PR changes, as the PR description requires. No unrelated functional changes were found in the reviewed diffs of the two source files. The test file and changeset were taken from the change summary and were not inspected directly.
